html:
The Eastern Mono, also called the Owens Valley Paiute, are a Numic people of the Owens Valley and the nearby mountains on the east side of the Sierra Nevada in California. The Monache, or Western Mono, who live across the Sierra on its western slope, speak the same language.

In their dry valley they dug ditches to flood stands of wild food plants, a rare kind of irrigation among people who did not farm, and they gathered pine nuts and seeds. Ranchers came in the 1860s, leading to the Owens Valley War of 1862 to 1863, after which hundreds were marched to Fort Tejon; many later came back to work on ranches. In the early 1900s Los Angeles bought up the valley's water rights and built the Los Angeles Aqueduct, which dried up Owens Lake. Their neighbours were the Tübatulabal to the south and the Western Shoshone and Northern Paiute to the east and north.
